sources.entry: Hyperconsciousness - Developer-alpha Rust knowledge store with encrypted, append-only records and an MCP server for agent access through scoped, expiring grants. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: HC (hyperconsciousness) is a developer-alpha, encrypted, append-only knowledge store in Rust that one trusted node owns and that agents reach through scoped, expiring grants via an MCP/HTTP server.
summary.what_it_does: HC stores notes and imported records in an encrypted, append-only store, with a CLI named `hc` for writing, reading, searching, and checking status. Access is controlled by grants that specify record kinds, tags, sensitivity level, read or write scope, and an expiry (for example, one day of read-only access to notes tagged "demo"). An MCP server exposes tools such as search, recent, record, remember, files, and access requests, and an HTTP server offers OAuth/DPoP, capture, and owner-approval APIs. The README also describes an opt-in lexical relevance mode for multiword search, an audit and revoke command, and an optional local dashboard (HC Atlas) for inspecting storage, file metadata, identity, and grants. It includes an installer for macOS and Linux, a Windows ZIP option, and a catalog of ingestion skills for sources such as Slack, GitHub, and Google Workspace.
use_cases: give an AI agent time-limited read access to personal notes
keep an encrypted personal knowledge base
share a company knowledge store with members and agents
search notes and imported chats through MCP
audit and revoke agent access to a store
ingest chats and tools into a searchable store
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | sh  (macOS/Linux installer; URL missing from README)
git clone the repository, then: cargo build --release --locked
cd dashboard && bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run build && bun run start  (optional dashboard)
notable: Grant-based access: scoped, expiring permissions limit what an agent's MCP calls return
Append-only encrypted record format with signed records and integrity verification for MCP reads
Single trusted node model: other devices query it through its authenticated API
Ingestion skill catalog covering chats, Slack, Google Workspace, GitHub, CRM and more, installable into Codex or Claude Code skill folders
Background update checks at most every six hours for installer-managed copies, with opt-out
caveats: Developer alpha: APIs and commands may change, and no independent security audit is claimed
Grants do not sandbox a process that has access to the owner's OS account, files, or keys; hosted model providers can see plaintext returned through grants
Mac builds are not notarized, Linux builds need Ubuntu 24.04-compatible libraries, and Windows is supported via ZIP only; desktop, iOS, Android, and mobile apps are out of scope
